title: September 2021 Class College Final Supplementary Exam (Part 5 of 6)
unit: Comprehensive Nursing (Mental Health, Research, Midwifery, Family Planning)

sets.title: Set 1: Original Exam Questions
sets.description: The original MCQs from the September 2021 class College Final Supplementary Exam paper (Kenya Registered Nursing, sat 30 May 2024, Multiple Choice Questions, Q81 to Q100).

questions.text: Baby Lika, 28 months is brought to the clinic. The mother reports baby Lika to constantly rub the ear and pus draining from the ear for the last 3 weeks. According to IMNCI, the nurse classifies baby Lika’s illness as:
questions.explanation: Chronic ear infection (D) is correct because in IMNCI pus draining from the ear for 14 days or more is classified as a chronic ear infection, and the treatment is to dry the ear by wicking, and refer if indicated, with follow-up after 5 days. Acute ear infection (A) is incorrect because it is pus draining for less than 14 days or ear pain, treated with an antibiotic for 5 days and dry ear wicking. Mastoiditis (B) is incorrect because it needs tender swelling behind the ear, and is a pink (urgent referral) classification. Otitis externa (C) is incorrect because it is not an IMNCI classification.

questions.text: The therapy of choice for alcoholism, sexual deviances, and smoking is:
questions.explanation: Aversion (A) is correct because aversion therapy pairs the unwanted behaviour (drinking alcohol, a deviant sexual stimulus, smoking) with an unpleasant stimulus (for example a drug such as disulfiram that causes vomiting or an electric shock), so that the person learns to associate the behaviour with discomfort and stops it. Classical conditioning (B) is incorrect because it is the learning principle on which aversion therapy is based, and not the therapy itself. Modelling (C) is incorrect because the person learns by observing a model, used for example for social skills and phobias. Behavioural conditioning (D) is incorrect because it is a general term and not the named therapy.

questions.text: A patient is gradually exposed to phobias that create extreme fear. Then learn relaxation strategies and begin exposing themselves to distressing situations while using techniques to cope. This therapy is:
questions.explanation: Systematic desensitization (B) is correct because in this therapy (Wolpe) the patient first learns relaxation techniques and then is exposed step by step to the feared situation, from the least to the most frightening (a fear hierarchy), while staying relaxed, so that the fear response is gradually extinguished. Flooding (A) is incorrect because the patient is exposed immediately and for a prolonged time to the most feared stimulus until the anxiety subsides. Implosion (C) is incorrect because it is flooding in imagination, in which the patient imagines the most feared scene vividly. Modelling desensitization (D) is incorrect because the patient learns by watching a model who handles the feared object without anxiety.

questions.text: Waxy flexibility is a motor feature common in the following disorder:
questions.explanation: Schizophrenia (C) is correct because waxy flexibility (cerea flexibilitas) is a catatonic feature in which the limbs of the patient stay in the position in which they are placed, like soft wax, and it occurs in catatonic schizophrenia together with stupor, mutism, posturing and negativism. Bipolar disorder (A) is incorrect as the best answer because catatonia can occur in severe mood disorders, but it is classically described in schizophrenia. Anxiety (B) is incorrect because it has autonomic and psychological symptoms but no catatonic signs. Delirium tremens (D) is incorrect because it presents with confusion, tremors, hallucinations and autonomic overactivity in alcohol withdrawal.

questions.text: The most likely diagnosis for Mr. Zee who prefers to shop at night in the supermarket to avoid being in crowds and standing in a queue because both cause him marked anxiety is:
questions.explanation: Agoraphobia (A) is correct because it is fear and avoidance of places or situations from which escape might be difficult, such as crowds, queues, public transport and open or crowded places, and the person avoids them or goes at quiet times. Social phobia (B) is incorrect because it is fear of being embarrassed or judged by others in social situations such as public speaking. Panic disorder (C) is incorrect because it is recurrent unexpected panic attacks, with worry about having more attacks. Claustrophobia (D) is incorrect because it is fear of enclosed spaces (lifts, small rooms), and not crowds and queues.

questions.text: The recommended mood stabilizer in bipolar disorder is:
questions.explanation: Lithium carbonate (A) is correct because it is the classic first-line mood stabiliser for the prevention and treatment of mania and bipolar disorder, and it needs monitoring of serum lithium levels (0.6 to 1.2 mmol/L), the kidney and thyroid function, and adequate salt and fluid intake, because toxicity causes coarse tremor, vomiting, diarrhoea and confusion. Olanzapine (B), haloperidol (C) and risperidone (D) are incorrect because they are antipsychotics, which are used to control acute mania or psychosis, and are not the recommended mood stabiliser (other mood stabilisers are sodium valproate and carbamazepine).

questions.text: A probability sampling design that involves selecting the Kth Participant is:
questions.explanation: Systematic (B) is correct because in systematic sampling the researcher calculates the sampling interval (k = population size divided by the sample size), picks a random starting point and then selects every kth person from the sampling frame. Cluster (A) is incorrect because groups (clusters) such as schools or villages are randomly selected. Convenience (C) and purposive (D) are incorrect because they are non-probability designs, in which participants are selected because they are easily available or because they have particular characteristics.

questions.text: A researcher is guilty of plagiarism if he:

options.A: Makes use of the works of others to gather information
options.B: Uses the work of another and misrepresent it as own
options.C: Makes use of the works of others to support own arguments
options.D: Examines the ideas and arguments of others to help shape own thoughts

questions.explanation: Uses the work of another and misrepresent it as own (B) is correct because plagiarism is presenting the words, ideas or data of another person as your own without acknowledging the source, which is research misconduct. Options A, C and D are incorrect because using, citing and examining the work of others to gather information, to support one's arguments and to shape one's thoughts is the normal literature review practice, and it is acceptable when the sources are properly acknowledged and referenced.

questions.text: The cardinal signs and symptoms of pre-eclampsia include:
questions.explanation: Proteinuria, high blood pressure, oedema (C) is correct because the classic triad of pre-eclampsia is hypertension (140/90 mmHg or more after 20 weeks), proteinuria (300 mg or more in 24 hours, or 1+ on dipstick) and generalised oedema (particularly of the face and hands). High blood pressure, oliguria, proteinuria (A) is incorrect because oliguria is a sign of severe disease. Epigastric pain, drowsiness, oedema (B) and headache, blurred vision, vomiting (D) are incorrect because epigastric pain, severe headache, visual disturbance and vomiting are symptoms of severe pre-eclampsia that warn of impending eclampsia, and they are not the cardinal triad.

questions.text: Multigravida is a woman who:

options.A: Has been pregnant more than once
options.D: Has given birth more than once

questions.explanation: Has been pregnant more than once (A) is correct because gravida refers to the number of pregnancies regardless of the outcome, so a multigravida has been pregnant two or more times. Has had multiple deliveries (B) and has given birth more than once (D) are incorrect because they describe a multipara (parity refers to births after 28 weeks, or the viable births). Has had multiple pregnancies (C) is incorrect because it means twins or more in one pregnancy.

questions.text: A true pelvis comprises of:
questions.explanation: Brim, cavity, outlet (D) is correct because the true (lesser) pelvis is the bony canal below the pelvic brim (the linea terminalis) through which the fetus passes in labour, and it has three parts: the inlet (brim), the cavity and the outlet. Options A, B and C are incorrect because each includes structures (side walls, ischial spines, sciatic notch, fore pelvis) that are landmarks or parts of the pelvis, but they are not the three divisions of the true pelvis. The false pelvis lies above the brim and supports the pregnant uterus.

questions.text: The causes of antepartum hemorrhage include:
questions.explanation: Placenta praevia, placenta abruptio (A) is correct because antepartum haemorrhage is bleeding from the genital tract after 28 weeks (24 weeks in some definitions) and before the delivery of the baby, and its two main causes are placenta praevia (low-lying placenta, painless bright red bleeding) and placental abruption (premature separation, painful bleeding with a hard tender uterus). Scar tissue (B) and uterine scar (D) are incorrect because they relate to scar dehiscence or rupture, which is a rarer cause in labour. Atonic uterus (C) and lacerations (D) are incorrect because they are causes of postpartum haemorrhage.

questions.text: Frequency of increased micturition in late pregnancy is due to:

options.C: Laxity of the pelvic floor muscles

questions.explanation: Reduced bladder space by gravidity (D) is correct because in the first trimester the frequency is from hormonal effects and the pressure of the growing uterus, and in late pregnancy it is because the presenting part engages and the heavy uterus presses on the bladder, so the bladder capacity falls and it fills quickly. Quickening (A) is incorrect because it is the mother's first perception of fetal movements at 16 to 20 weeks. Onset of labour (B) is incorrect because frequency is a feature of the late third trimester, and not a sign of labour. Laxity of the pelvic floor muscles (C) is incorrect because it contributes to stress incontinence but is not the main cause of frequency.

questions.text: The following would make the fundal height abnormally high during pregnancy:
questions.explanation: Polyhydramnios, multiple pregnancy (B) is correct because both conditions over-distend the uterus, so the fundal height is larger than expected for the gestational age (other causes are a large baby from diabetes, a wrong date and fibroids). Transverse lie, longitudinal lie (A) is incorrect because a transverse lie makes the fundal height smaller than expected, and a longitudinal lie is the normal lie. Breech presentation, cephalic presentation (C) is incorrect because presentation does not significantly alter the fundal height. Pre-eclampsia, obesity (D) is incorrect because pre-eclampsia is associated with intrauterine growth restriction (a small fundal height), and obesity makes measurement difficult but does not enlarge the uterus.

questions.text: Management of cord presentation include:

options.A: Discouraging premature pushing, sedating the mother
options.B: Rupture of membranes, relieving pressure on the cord
options.C: Positioning mother on knee chest position, starting intravenous infusion
options.D: Rupturing the membranes, assessing cervical dilatation

questions.explanation: Positioning mother on knee chest position, starting intravenous infusion (C) is correct because in a cord presentation (the cord lies below the presenting part with the membranes intact) the aim is to prevent the cord from being compressed or prolapsing, so the mother is placed in the knee-chest or the exaggerated Sims position (head down, buttocks up), the membranes are kept intact, an IV line is started, the fetal heart is monitored and the mother is prepared for an emergency caesarean section. Options A, B and D are incorrect because rupturing the membranes (B and D) is contraindicated, since it would convert the presentation into a prolapse, and sedating the mother (A) does not help.

questions.text: A reflex present when the nurses gently touch the corner of the newborn’s mouth and the baby open the mouth turning towards the stimuli is:
questions.explanation: Rooting (A) is correct because stroking the cheek or the corner of the mouth makes the baby turn the head toward the stimulus and open the mouth, which helps the baby to find the nipple for feeding (it disappears at about 3 to 4 months). Babinski (B) is incorrect because the toes fan out when the sole of the foot is stroked. Sucking (C) is incorrect because the baby sucks when an object is placed in the mouth or touches the roof of the mouth. Moro (D) is incorrect because the baby extends and then draws in the arms in response to a sudden loss of support or a loud noise.

questions.text: After delivery, the nurses prepares to prevent heat loss in the newborn resulting from evaporation by:

options.B: Closing the door to the room
options.C: Turing on the overhead radiant warmer
options.D: Drying the infant in a warm blanket

questions.explanation: Drying the infant in a warm blanket (D) is correct because evaporation is heat lost when moisture (amniotic fluid) on the wet skin changes to vapour, so the baby is dried immediately after birth, the wet linen is removed and the baby is wrapped in dry warm cloths with the head covered. Warming the crib pad (A) is incorrect because it prevents conduction (heat lost by contact with a cold surface). Closing the door to the room (B) is incorrect because it prevents convection (heat lost to moving air currents). Turning on the overhead radiant warmer (C) is incorrect because it prevents radiation (heat lost to cooler objects that are not in contact with the baby).

questions.text: Contraceptive Patch:

options.B: May be applied on the breast
options.C: Are applied throughout the year without a break
options.D: Is applied every week for 3 weeks

questions.explanation: Is applied every week for 3 weeks (D) is correct because the combined contraceptive patch is applied once a week for 3 weeks (a new patch each week on the same day), followed by a patch-free week in which withdrawal bleeding occurs, and then a new cycle is started. Releases progesterone only (A) is incorrect because it releases both oestrogen and progestogen. May be applied on the breast (B) is incorrect because it can be applied to the buttocks, upper outer arm, abdomen or upper torso, but not the breasts. Applied throughout the year without a break (C) is incorrect because of the patch-free week in each 4-week cycle.

questions.text: Progesterone releasing vaginal contraceptive ring:

options.A: Is left in situ for 3 weeks
options.B: Decreases risk of transmission of HIV/AIDS
options.C: Should be inserted by the health care provider
options.D: Is effective in active breast feeding

questions.explanation: Is effective in active breast feeding (D) is correct because the progesterone-releasing vaginal ring (PVR) is designed for breastfeeding women, who can use it from 4 weeks after delivery, and the progestogen does not reduce the milk supply, with the contraceptive effect enhanced by the lactational amenorrhoea. Is left in situ for 3 weeks (A) is incorrect because the combined ring is left for 3 weeks, followed by a ring-free week, while the progesterone ring is left in for about 3 months (90 days) and then replaced by a new ring. Decreases risk of transmission of HIV/AIDS (B) is incorrect because it gives no protection from sexually transmitted infections (a condom is needed). Should be inserted by the health care provider (C) is incorrect because the woman can insert and remove it herself.

questions.text: A client on combined oral contraceptive pills misses 3 pills in the second week. The nurse instructs the client to:

options.A: Discard the unused pills and start a new pack
options.B: Take a pill as soon as possible and use back up for 7 days
options.C: Take all the missed pills at once and reassure there is no risk of pregnancy

questions.explanation: Take a pill as soon as possible and use back up for 7 days (B) is correct because missing two or more combined pills puts the woman at risk of ovulation and pregnancy, so she takes the most recent missed pill as soon as she remembers (even if it means two pills in one day), continues the remaining pills at the usual time, and uses a condom or abstains for the next 7 days, and if the pills were missed in the third week she should skip the pill-free interval and start the next pack straight away. Emergency contraception is considered if there was unprotected sex. Discarding the pack and starting a new one (A) is incorrect because it may leave a long gap. Taking all the missed pills at once (C) is incorrect because it causes nausea and does not remove the risk. Continuing as usual (D) is incorrect because there is a risk of pregnancy.
